{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Services Agreement (Clear Capital / RadialSpark)

**To:** Deal Team 
**From:** Legal (In-House Counsel) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Contractor services agreement — issues, positions and next steps

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Overall, the commercial structure is favourable to us in several respects: there is no exclusivity, no minimum purchase or volume commitment, no MFN burden, no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, no non-compete on our business lines, and no Vendor audit right against us. Those items are compliant and require no redline.

The risk is concentrated in the Vendor-facing protections. Three critical issues drive our position:

1. **No indemnity of any kind.** Section 7 is captioned "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains only liability caps and damages waivers — a document-wide search returns no operative indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language. Contractor's IP non-infringement warranty in § 5(c) is therefore unbacked, and we bear the cost of third-party infringement claims, Contractor-caused data breaches and Contractor misconduct. This is our walk-away scenario.
2. **Deliverable ownership is contingent on payment.** Under § 4(a), title to the Works does not vest on creation and there is no present assignment, leaving Contractor as owner of unpaid-for deliverables. There is also no provision confirming our ownership of Company Data and pre-existing IP, and no bar on joint ownership.
3. **The liability cap is illusory and asymmetric.** The § 7(a) cap is "fees paid" for the particular SOW, with no 12-month or USD floor, and the only carve-out points to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor) — so confidentiality breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all sit inside a potentially trivial cap.

High-severity gaps follow in termination for convenience (Contractor may exit on 15 days' notice; we have no convenience exit while an SOW is live), assignment (no affiliate/successor carve-out), and licence scope (the § 4(c) licence runs to "Company" alone, is not irrevocable and is not transferable). Medium and low items — governing law/arbitration, transition assistance, performance warranty, rate escalation, non-solicit carve-outs and insurance limits — are addressable with standard language and sensible fallbacks.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / Ask |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Insert Contractor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard defence procedure and carve-out from the cap (new § 7(d)). |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Works vest in Company on creation with express irrevocable assignment; add Company Data/pre-existing IP ownership and no joint ownership; make the embedded-Contractor-IP licence irrevocable and worldwide. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; add standard Excluded Claims carve-outs; confirm fee payment obligations are not capped damages. § 7(b) consequential waiver is already compliant and left unchanged. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Add Company affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, bar assignment to a Company competitor, and confirm a Company change of control is not an assignment and creates no Contractor termination or re-pricing right. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 Termination | Give Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW with pro-rata refund and no penalty; confine Contractor's convenience right to periods with no outstanding SOW on 90 days' notice (15 days is below walk-away). |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Extend the § 4(c) licence to Company affiliates and contractors, make it irrevocable, and make it transferable to a successor to our business or assets. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; engagement is task-by-task via SOWs on time and materials. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 6 Termination | No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination fees; recovery limited to fees and expenses incurred or earned. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | No covenant restricts our business lines or fields of use; the only restrictive covenant is the mutual employee non-solicit. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Change governing law from Arizona to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. Not a walk-away (domestic seat). |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 Termination | Insert new § 6(d): six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable data return, certified deletion, carved back for Contractor's Information under § 4(b). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 5 Contractor's Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer | Add new § 5(f): workmanship, conformity to Specifications and no-malicious-code warranties with repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, and confirm § 5(e) does not swallow the express warranties. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Price predictability | Deviation | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No auto-renewal issue (evergreen term, 15-day exit). Cap Contractor's unilateral rate increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, once per 12 months, on 60 days' notice; rates fixed during each SOW. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Clause is mutual, Services-personnel-limited and 12 months. Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs only (minimal fallback edit). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No Vendor audit, inspection or records-examination right exists. No redline (adding a framework would create a right Vendor does not have). |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation binds us. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | Pure time and materials for Services actually ordered; no minimum, shortfall or take-or-pay exposure. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Raise E&O to USD 2M, add USD 2M CGL aggregate, add USD 5M cyber/privacy cover, and extend coverage one year past term. Fallback: E&O USD 1M plus cyber USD 2M. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

1. **No Vendor indemnity (INDEMN, § 7).** The complete absence of any indemnity, defence or hold-harmless obligation is the identified walk-away scenario. We cannot accept an unbacked IP non-infringement warranty while carrying the cost of third-party infringement claims and Contractor-caused data breaches. Our insertion of a Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d), carved out from the § 7 caps, is not negotiable in principle.
2. **Contractor's 15-day convenience termination (T4C, § 6(a)).** Fifteen days' notice is below the playbook walk-away threshold of 90 days. Contractor's convenience right must be confined to periods with no outstanding SOW and extended to 90 days' notice.

We note for completeness that the Arizona law / arbitration point (GOVLAW) is a deviation but **not** a walk-away, as the arbitration seat is domestic rather than foreign.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eleven deviation/missing items above; the seven compliant items are left untouched, as are § 7(b) (consequential damages waiver) and § 4(b) (Contractor's retention of its pre-existing tools and methodologies), which already meet our position.
2. **Lead the negotiation on the three critical items** — Vendor indemnity, deliverable/data ownership and the liability cap — as a package. The cap carve-outs and the indemnity are interdependent; conceding on either separately weakens both.
3. **Hold firm on the two walk-away items** and escalate internally before conceding on the absence of an indemnity or on Contractor's 15-day convenience exit.
4. **Deploy the identified fallbacks where useful to close:** 90/30-day warranty periods (WARRANTY); a 5% rate-increase cap (RENEWAL); affiliate coverage on notice with M&A successor transfer only (LICENSE); and E&O USD 1M plus cyber USD 2M (INSURANCE).
5. **Confirm the verification status.** All findings are recorded as verification "skipped"; we will re-run validation on the drafted redline before it goes out. The ASSIGN redline has already validated clean.
6. **Flag the cyber exposure to the business.** Contractor receives Company Confidential Information including data and records, may access our systems and works at our facilities — which is why cyber/privacy cover, the data-return and certified-deletion obligations, and the confidentiality carve-out from the cap should be treated as a linked set."}
